entries.buyer_decision: How much virgin material a multi-stage recovery chain still needs, and whether adding a stage is worth more than improving the best one.
entries.proven: For recovery fractions in [0,1], the virgin share is the product of (1 - r), lies in [0,1], is at least (1 - max r)^n, is never above the best single stage, and is strictly below it when another stage recovers anything.
entries.assumed: Stages act in series on one material, each recovering a fixed fraction of what reaches it; no losses between stages, downgrading or rebound demand; the fractions supplied are the real ones.
entries.reason: Extends the live loop-mass-balance service, which takes one recovery fraction, with a proven bound for chains of several recovery stages (class B).

entries.buyer_decision: How much virgin material a one-material recovery loop will still need over a planning horizon at a chosen recovery fraction, and what secondary stock to plan storage for.
entries.proven: For demand D >= 0, recovery fraction r in [0,1] and stock retention rho in [0,1), the virgin input per period D(1 - r) lies between 0 and D; the secondary stock gap to r D / (1 - rho) shrinks as rho^t and the stock converges to that level; the virgin total over T periods is T D (1 - r); and for D > 0, T > 0 that total strictly falls as r rises.
entries.assumed: One material; demand, recovery fraction and retention are constant over the horizon; recovery is not capped by the stock actually available; no quality losses, rebound demand or price effects; the numbers supplied are the real ones.
entries.reason: A new service: no live kernel plans virgin input and secondary stock for a recovery loop (class A).
